mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained high unemployment (>5% for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of persistent industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% combined with a concurrent increase in savings rate (RSAFS) signals a shift toward precautionary savings, which reduces household financial risk-taking and equity demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND RSAFS > previous 6-month average for 1 month
regime_hint: post-crisis or monetary easing with rising savings
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in personal income growth (implied by PAYEMS) alongside a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two months signals demand-pull inflation, which increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% AND PAYEMS growth > previous 6-month average for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of accelerating income and high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of very low unemployment (<3.5% for 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining GDP growth (GDPC1), signals a buildup of precautionary balances that reduces equity market participation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for 6 consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes of rising savings and weak GDP growth.
